A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ResDec. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be reliably matched across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, ablations, efficiency measurements, and qualitative case studies across several LVLMs.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds historical-window selection and aggregation ablations in Appendix C.2-C.3.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same JSD-based historical-window selection, confidence-weighted aggregation, residual blending, and vocabulary constraint. The new appendix experiments test alternatives without changing the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: The eleven benchmarks and their task coverage remain unchanged. The new ablations use POPE and MME, both already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: Tables 8-9 add full-window, individual-phase, top-four-confidence, uniform-pooling, and distance-decay comparators. The external baseline membership in the retained benchmark and efficiency comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix C.2-C.3 introduces controlled comparisons varying historical-phase selection and aggregation on Qwen2.5-VL and LLaVA-1.5. Existing splits, metrics, model configurations, and decoding settings are not revised.

E4.justification: The revision adds direct ablations of both central design choices: selecting SAP plus EDP and using confidence-weighted aggregation. Tables 8-9 test competing choices across two models and two benchmarks, substantially extending v1's parameter-sensitivity and decoding-strategy analyses.

E5.justification: Figure 3 retains its mean and standard-deviation display over 200 POPE-MSCOCO examples. The new ablation tables report point estimates; no run-count, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-test information is added.

E6.justification: Existing results in Tables 1-7 and the figures are unchanged. Tables 8-9 add variant results: for example, Qwen2.5-VL POPE accuracy is 88.82 for SAP-only and 88.31 for mean pooling, compared with the retained ResDec value of 90.16.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation in Section 3 and Appendix B's language-prior derivation, definitions, assumptions, two theorems, and proofs are retained without substantive revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free historical guidance, hallucination reduction, broad benchmark applicability, and negligible inference overhead. The additional ablations support existing contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix C.2-C.3 interprets the new comparisons through early-phase noise, useful EDP context, and better semantic isolation through confidence weighting than through fixed or distance-based weights. These are limited extensions of v1's existing mechanism rationale.

D1.justification: The new controls receive limited operational specifications: selecting four confident steps, averaging logits uniformly, and weighting by inverse temporal distance. Existing implementation disclosures, including alpha=0.5, beta=0.1, W=8, and Appendix A's dataset information, remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds 14 references, including TreeReview, Domaino1s, MORE-R1, and ShifCon, mainly within existing introductory and related-work citation groups. All earlier references remain, and the substantive positioning of ResDec is unchanged.

P1.justification: There are small abstract and efficiency-paragraph edits and updated author contribution, correspondence, and affiliation markers. Appendix C becomes Additional Ablation Studies, retaining the previous window-length discussion as C.1 and adding C.2-C.3; the main narrative is largely unchanged.

P2.justification: Tables 8-9 are newly added. Existing tables and figures retain their content and design, with local text reflow, shifted appendix pages, and removal of page-number footers.

improvement.justification: v1 motivated phase selection and confidence weighting without directly comparing these alternatives; v3's Tables 8-9 supply those controls on two models and two benchmarks. This strengthens empirical support for the design. The gain remains limited because the broader evaluation and uncertainty reporting are unchanged.
